A quoted setup time is preserved exactly as written; timezone is not inferred unless the message states it.
A technically valid RB is kept separate from an actionable trade.
Message co-mention counts are descriptive coverage, not win rates or causal estimates.

identification.statement: The corpus treats an RB as a rejection of something meaningful, commonly a liquidity event, PD array, key level, or imbalance; it is not every wick.
identification.caveat: The most complete checklist is peer-written. Domme's direct reply confirms volume imbalance for a specific chart but does not supply a universal definition.

identification.statement: Close confirmation matters. In one classification Domme required a bearish close; in another trade validation he said to wait for the RB to close.
The prior candle's color alone is not presented as disqualifying; one recap accepted a 4h RB with a bullish prior candle because it was a swing low with a wick.
A marking from the previous candle close to the next candle's wick was justified by Domme through the volume imbalance in that example.
Timeframe choice is selective: a poor-looking 1m RB immediately before a 15m candle open was rejected, and Domme directly said he would not take a 10m-chart RB.
CE/start-of-RB and lower-timeframe entry triggers are both used, but the corpus does not contain a canonical rule choosing between them.

invalidation_and_non_actionability.statement: Do not act while the RB is merely forming; the cited guidance requires the relevant close.
An already-mitigated RB is treated as non-actionable for the proposed entry.
An RB can remain technically valid while the trade is no longer attractive because the daily draw has already delivered.
If the planned key level is not fully tapped, the RB entry is passed; examples cite an incomplete 10am tap and missing 00:00/FVG-CE taps.

Stops are commonly placed beyond the RB wick/structure. If a large wick forces an arbitrary stop inside the wick, the journal evidence treats the risk definition as invalid even if the RB idea exists.
Bias conflict can invalidate the trade plan even when the author calls the RB and fib technically valid.
Skipping the planned 30s/1m confirmation or entering before the deeper PDA tap produced immediate losses in the cited journal.
A stacked NQ/ES setup can still be low quality when the other index has unresolved liquidity; one A- trade failed until ES swept its data low.
A member records Powell saying RBs that begin an unfilled imbalance are not good entries.

The corpus supports a stop beyond the wick/structure but does not contain a direct authoritative answer defining exactly when an RB itself ceases to exist after later closes, CE interaction, or partial mitigation.

timing.statement: 10am is the dominant setup-time anchor in the RB primary corpus: 67 of 201 RB-containing primary messages mention 10am/10:00/10KO. This is a mention count, not an occurrence or win-rate estimate.
For the 10am model, the cited sequence is to let price fully tap the 10am level before entry, and Domme stops looking at 11am.
9:30/market-open context is the next most common explicit timing family (18 of 201 messages). A concrete recap has a 3m RB at 9:57 and 1m entry at 10:04.
Other recurring anchors are 00:00/midnight (8 messages), 18:00/1800 (6), Asia (6), and London (4). Domme specifically says 3-5am if he trades London.
Only one corpus rule excerpt explicitly labels 10am as EST. Other setup times are retained as written and are not timezone-normalized.
All evidence timestamps in this artifact are Discord post times in UTC; they are not treated as the time the RB appeared unless the message text explicitly gives a setup time.

high_probability_profile.statement: The strongest repeated profile starts with a meaningful rejection and higher-timeframe bias/PDA support, not an isolated lower-timeframe wick.
Higher-timeframe RB/FVG or OB, then 5m/15m RB, then a closed 1m/30s trigger is the clearest repeated high-quality structure.
The most common model cluster is 10am plus FVG/OB/RB and OTE/fib, usually after manipulation and with the full level reached.
SMT, often with ES, is treated as an additional confirmation rather than a standalone setup; Domme says a 1m SMT is better to have.
Waiting for the RB/trigger close and defining the stop beyond actual structure improves the setup profile; tighter timeframes are conditional, not automatically better.
A valid pattern is higher quality while the intended draw remains open; once the daily low has delivered, Domme treats the RB as valid but the trade as exhausted.

low_probability_profile.statement: A poor-looking 1m RB, especially just before a 15m candle open or from a random imbalance, is low quality.
Trading against bias or repeatedly flipping bias to force participation is a strong loss profile even when SMT/RB/fib are present.
Already-mitigated RBs and RBs after the target has delivered are non-actionable or lower probability.
A very large wick, an arbitrary stop inside it, or a skipped lower-timeframe confirmation produces repeated loss/edge-out behavior.
Consolidation, decorrelated NQ/ES behavior, or an unswept opposing index level can overwhelm otherwise stacked confluences.
FED/news volatility appears in loss examples even with 1h FVG, 5m RB, SMT and 0.79 alignment; confluence count alone did not protect the trade.
An RB that forms before the full planned 10am or PDA tap is lower quality for that model.

instrument_profile.statement: The corpus does not establish that RBs work best on NQ. It contains RB use on both NQ and ES, with 27 NQ/MNQ mentions, 30 ES/MES mentions, and 19 messages mentioning both families; no head-to-head win-rate denominator is available.
A common pattern is NQ execution or RB context paired with ES as SMT or an aligned higher-timeframe gap/RB, rather than requiring identical blocks on both charts.
instrument_profile.caveat: The direct question asking whether ES must also form the RB was unanswered, so identical-block requirements remain unresolved.

instrument_profile.statement: MNQ and NQ can print materially different taps around CE. One loss review says MNQ tapped while NQ edged the 15m RB CE, changing the author's interpretation.
For NQ/ES liquidity sweeps of only one or two ticks, boy and Domme answered that a sweep is a sweep and that such setups can work.
MES is not mentioned in the 201 RB primary messages, so no MES-specific conclusion is supported.

qa_catalog.answer: Yes in the chart asked about: Domme said it was an RB if it closed bearish.

qa_catalog.question: Must the trigger RB close before entry?
qa_catalog.answer: Domme approved the setup if the trader waited for the RB to close.

qa_catalog.question: Why was the 1m RB inside the 15m FVG rejected?
qa_catalog.answer: Domme disliked the RB shape and noted it was immediately before a 15m candle open; he wanted the prior 15m low taken first.

qa_catalog.question: Would Domme take an RB from the 10m chart?

Is 1m SMT useful for RB entries?
qa_catalog.answer: Domme said it is better if SMT is present, but did not quantify fakeout risk or make it mandatory.

qa_catalog.question: Does a one- or two-tick NQ/ES liquidity sweep require a resweep?
qa_catalog.answer: boy said a sweep is a sweep; Domme said such sweeps can work.

qa_catalog.question: Why could the RB be drawn from the prior close to the next wick?
qa_catalog.answer: Domme cited the volume imbalance. The answer did not provide a general drawing algorithm.

qa_catalog.question: Does an RB have to be created by a liquidity sweep?
qa_catalog.note: A peer says yes; the direct question has no captured mentor answer.

qa_catalog.question: Is an RB still valid if the following candle closes bullish?
If lower-timeframe engineered liquidity sits at CE while the original-timeframe CE is unmitigated, is wick theory valid?
If price closes below OTE but respects an RB to the left, is the range invalid or should the RB hold?
How should a trader choose a 10am limit entry versus an entry model?
Should 5m/15m RBs be entered at start/CE or via 30s/1m entry trigger?
Must ES form the same RB for a 5m NQ RB to be valid?
Do RBs work better on NQ than ES?
qa_catalog.answer: Both instruments appear in RB analysis, but the corpus lacks a trade-level instrument denominator and comparable outcomes.

contradictions_and_tensions.description: Peer teaching states a sweep is required, while a direct Domme answer validates a specific marking because of volume imbalance. No captured authoritative answer resolves whether every RB needs a liquidity sweep.
Poor 1m RBs are explicitly rejected, yet 1m/30s triggers appear in the strongest wins. The evidence supports conditional use, not a blanket ban.
SMT is described as better to have and appears in wins, but a stacked SMT/RB trade failed while ES still had unresolved liquidity.
Domme can call an RB valid while rejecting the trade because the daily draw already delivered; pattern validity is not trade validity.
Wins show nested RB/FVG/OTE/SMT stacks, but losses show similar stacks defeated by bias conflict, bad stop geometry, news, or unresolved ES liquidity.
ES is repeatedly used as confirmation for NQ, but NQ and ES can disrespect/hold different RBs and the direct same-RB requirement is unanswered.

strongest_examples.why_it_is_strong_in_corpus_terms: Nested higher/lower timeframe structure, fib/key-open alignment, and a lower-timeframe trigger.
The entry followed a complete contextual sequence instead of treating the RB alone as the setup.
RB plus correlated-market confirmation, reversal trigger, target, and explicit risk plan.
Multiple timeframes and instruments aligned after displacement rather than anticipation.

strongest_examples.outcome: missed/no trade; chart later reached full TP for 7R
strongest_examples.why_it_is_strong_in_corpus_terms: Useful model evidence, but not an executed win and must not be counted in win rate.

weakest_examples.failure_profile: Risk geometry did not cover the actual wick, and the author later questioned the repeated OTE/rally narrative.
The setup was opposite the author's bias; technical confluences did not override narrative conflict.
The author skipped the planned 30s confirmation and later said price needed a deeper 15m-gap tap.
ES still wanted its own data low; stacked confluences did not resolve opposing correlated liquidity.
News volatility and fill/plan problems made the otherwise stacked setup unreliable.
Complicated price action, forced participation, and repeated bias flipping.

limitations.limitation: No normalized trade ledger exists in the export. One message may contain several trades, edits, screenshots, or a hypothetical setup, so a defensible RB win rate cannot be computed.
The broad server-wide RB shorthand search is partial at 325 results. The complete primary channel and complete phrase/question searches reduce but do not eliminate missing context.
Some contextual messages have blank authors in the export. They are labeled unresolved_in_export and are not treated as authoritative unless a named reply supplies the conclusion.
Screenshots were not visually classified in this artifact. Text-only excerpts cannot verify whether a wick, FVG, CE, SMT, or stop was drawn correctly.
Most setup times lack an explicit timezone. Only the freemium 10am rule excerpt states EST; Discord post timestamps are UTC and must not be substituted for setup time.

NQ versus ES performance cannot be ranked because the corpus lacks instrument-specific denominators, standardized outcomes, and consistent distinction between signal instrument and execution instrument.

llm_use_notes: Resolve evidence_refs through evidence_catalog before presenting any conclusion.
Prefer direct mentor replies over freemium peer definitions when they conflict.
Never turn co-mention counts into a probability or win rate.
Keep valid_pattern, actionable_trade, and outcome as separate fields in downstream answers.
Treat hypothetical/missed full-TP examples as model evidence, not wins.
State 'not established by this corpus' for a comparative NQ-versus-ES edge.
